BILL NUMBER:  S3749

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, the general municipal law
and the public officers law, in relation to adjudications and owner
liability for a violation of traffic-control signal indications and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :
This bill authorizes. Nassau County to adopt a local law that would
allow for the installation of traffic control signal photo violation
monitoring systems ("Red Light Cameras") at up to fifty intersections
throughout the county and provide for violations not to exceed fifty
dollars thereof.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1: Makes technical and conforming changes.

Section 2: Prohibits the registration or renewal of a motor vehicle
application if an applicant has three or more outstanding red light
camera violations under the foregoing provisions.

Section 3. Amends VTL section 1111 (b) to authorize Nassau County to
adopt a local law establishing a red light camera demonstration
program at fifty intersections throughout the county and imposing
monetary fines for violations thereof. The section further outlines
the parameters for establishment of such a program as well as penalty
provisions.

Section 4. Makes technical and conforming changes.

Section 5. Makes technical and conforming changes.

Section 6. Makes technical and conforming changes.

Section 7. Makes technical and conforming changes.

Section 8. Amends subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officers
law to include photographs, microphotographs, videotape or other
recorded images prepared under authority of section 1111 (b) of the
VTL.

Section 9. Makes the purchase or lease of equipment for establishment
of red light camera programs subject to section 103 of the general
municipal law.

Section 10: Establishes the effective date and sunset of such program.

 EXISTING LAW :
New York city is currently the only municipality authorized to have a
demonstration program utilizing red light cameras.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 1988 the New York State legislature enacted legislation that
allowed New York city to establish a demonstration program to install
photo monitoring devices to record vehicles going through red light
signals at traffic intersections. "Red Light Camera Programs" have
proven to be an effective traffic safety measure that prevent injuries
and the loss of life due to accidents caused by red light running.

Since its inception in December of 1993, hundreds of thousands of
vehicles, including buses and taxicabs, have been caught going through
red lights by the traffic control monitoring devices in New York city.
In calendar year 2005 alone, 306,117 violations or Notices of
Liability ("NOLs") were issued to violators.
A large number of traffic accidents resulting in bodily injury and
death to motorists, passengers, pedestrians and bicyclists are due to
the failure of motorists to obey traffic control signals located at
intersections.  "Right angle" and pedestrian accidents accidents
attributed to red light running are among the leading causes of
traffic fatalities. By reducing the number of vehicles running red
lights, the likelihood of "right angle" and and pedestrian accidents
is reduced. The extended use of these devices has been shown to
dramatically reduce the number of violations at the intersections
being monitored.

Red Light Camera Programs have proven to be an effective traffic
safety initiative whose success has been recognized by the State
Legislature and the New York City Council in their repeated
authorizations to extend the initial demonstration program. This
legislation would seek to expand the current program to Nassau county
to further promote safety and decrease motor vehicle accidents.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill will increase revenue for Nassau county through the
placement of red light cameras at intersections throughout the county
should a local law be adopted to establish such a program.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire on December 1, 2014.

summary: Relates to adjudications and owner liability for a violation of traffic-control signal indications in Nassau county.
